title: Three common types of linked lists
summary: Compare the link structures of singly, circular, and doubly linked lists using the same nodes 1, 3, 2, 5, and 4.
context: All three rows use five nodes arranged in the order 1, 3, 2, 5, 4, comparing the three connection patterns from top to bottom.

frames.title: Three common types of linked lists
frames.explanation: A singly linked list can only be traversed forward along successor references; in a circular linked list, any node can serve as the head; a doubly linked list can be traversed in both directions via next or prev, at the cost of storing an extra predecessor reference.

tables.caption: References and boundaries of the three linked list types
rows: Tail node 4 has next pointing to None
Tail node 4 routes back beneath the row to node 1, forming a closed loop
Node order is 1, 3, 2, 5, 4; between every adjacent pair, rightward next points to the successor and leftward prev points to the predecessor
Node 1 has prev pointing to None on the left, and node 4 has next pointing to None on the right
